I will still farm the way I know works here in Quzhou: I start from what I did last year, then I adjust a little for cost and for the weather. I have only 10.1 mu, so I cannot gamble. Wheat and maize are still my backbone, because that wheat-maize rotation is what our land and our water setup can carry best. I will keep 6.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, then use 2 mu for cotton and 2 mu for stevia. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a little on fertilizer and lose yield, that loss is bigger than the saving. So for wheat I will keep the base fertilizer solid, because wheat needs a strong stand before winter and enough ears next spring. For maize I will push nitrogen a bit more, because maize shows quickly if the leaves go pale and then the ear gets short. For cotton I will not overdo nitrogen, or it runs to stalk and leaves and delays boll opening. For stevia, I will feed it steadily and keep water on time, because leaf yield is what brings money. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage instead of waiting on the sky. I also watch what nearby farmers do. Around here, people who get stable yield do not use the very cheapest seed. So I will use improved wheat, hybrid maize, better cotton seed, and improved stevia seedlings. I will use rotary tillage on most ground because it saves labor for my age and my family size, and it is enough for this scale.
